## Observations

1. The input is a single valid direction code containing one or two letters.
2. Reversing a direction swaps N with S and E with W, without changing the order of the letters in the code.
3. Each letter replacement takes constant time, and there are at most two letters to replace.

## Solution sketch

> The input is a single valid direction code containing one or two letters.

1. Read the input line and remove its trailing newline. No validation is needed because the input is guaranteed to be a valid code.

> Reversing a direction swaps N with S and E with W, without changing the order of the letters in the code.

2. Visit each letter of the original code from left to right and append its opposite to the result. Print the resulting code. A one-letter direction needs only one replacement, as in N becoming S. For a diagonal, replace both letters in place order, so SE becomes NW.

> Each letter replacement takes constant time, and there are at most two letters to replace.

3. The algorithm uses O(1) time and O(1) space because the input and result are both bounded by two letters.
